Our current quiz platform is killing me, I would like to examine building a new quiz tool in Astro. Here are the notes. BTW I think the component should engineered so I can share it with the community. # Engineering Specification: Custom MDX-Driven Quiz Engine for Astro This specification defines the architecture and implementation requirements for a lightweight, code-driven quiz engine built natively inside an Astro project. It replaces the need for third-party marketing tools (ScoreApp/Interact) by utilizing a hybrid MDX configuration file for content portability, Git version control, and precise category sub-scoring. --- ## 1. System Overview & Architecture The quiz engine consists of three decoupled layers managed within the core Astro repository: 1. **Content Layer (MDX + Frontmatter):** Question schemas, answer weightings, and multi-tier outcome structures live inside the frontmatter of an MDX file. The rich text for the results pages, along with markdown footnotes, lives in the MDX body. 2. **Frontend Orchestrator Component (`client:load`):** A lightweight, client-side UI stepper handles sequential state management, validation, and browser history tracking (`popstate`) for back-button support. 3. **Backend Processing & Integration Layer (Astro Endpoint):** A server-side endpoint intercepts the quiz submission, processes the multi-tier diagnostic scoring, safely transforms variables, and pushes data to Cakemail via API/Webhook. --- ## 2. File & Directory Architecture Ensure your implementation creates or updates the following files: ```text src/ ├── content/ │ ├── config.ts # Zod schema validation for quiz frontmatter │ └── quizzes/ │ └── ai-tsunami.mdx # Single source of truth for quiz content & logic ├── components/ │ └── QuizStepper.svelte/tsx/vue # Client-side component for handling steps & state ├── pages/ │ ├── quiz/ │ │ ├── [slug].astro # Dynamic landing / execution page │ │ └── results.astro # Dynamic, server-rendered results page │ └── api/ │ └── quiz-submit.ts # Astro API route for scoring computation & Cakemail sync ``` --- ## 3. Data Models & Content Schema ### Zod Schema Definition (`src/content/config.ts`) The schema forces strict typing on questions, section categories, and outcome tier point bands. ```typescript import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content'; const quizzesCollection = defineCollection({ type: 'content', schema: z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string().optional(), sections: z.record(z.string(), z.string()), // e.g., { "infra": "Infrastructure & Data" } questions: z.array( z.object({ id: z.string(), section: z.string(), text: z.string(), options: z.array( z.object({ text: z.string(), score: z.number().int() }) ) }) ).length(12), // Strict validation for 12 questions outcomes: z.array( z.object({ tier: z.string(), // e.g., "low", "medium", "high" minScore: z.number().int(), maxScore: z.number().int(), title: z.string() }) ) }) }); export const collections = { quizzes: quizzesCollection }; ``` ### Hybrid Content Structure (`src/content/quizzes/ai-tsunami.mdx`) This file represents the absolute data and copy baseline. ```markdown --- title: "AI Tsunami Readiness Quiz" sections: infra: "Infrastructure & Data" team: "Team Capability" strategy: "Strategic Alignment" operations: "Operational Efficiency" questions: - id: "q1" section: "infra" text: "Where is your primary customer data stored?" options: - text: "Legacy on-prem servers" score: 1 - text: "Cloud data warehouse with dynamic syncing" score: 3 # [Repeat structured array pattern cleanly up to 12 questions] outcomes: - tier: "high-risk" minScore: 0 maxScore: 15 title: "High Risk" - tier: "moderate-risk" minScore: 16 maxScore: 28 title: "Moderate Risk" - tier: "ai-ready" minScore: 29 maxScore: 36 title: "AI Ready" --- export const components = {}; ## Results Segment Injection This section handles the rendering logic parsed by the results page. ### Tier: high-risk Your current setup indicates infrastructure vulnerabilities. According to recent performance indices, maintaining legacy data pipelines severely cripples continuous model fine-tuning[^1]. [^1]: Global AI Infrastructure Survey, Q1 2026. ### Tier: ai-ready Your enterprise displays robust structural elasticity. Focus on secondary operational automations. ``` --- ## 4. Execution Components & Technical Requirements ### Client-Side Stepper Logic Implement the wizard UI using a micro-framework island or heavily optimized Vanilla JavaScript. It must map exactly to these behavioral parameters: * **State Vector:** Maintain an internal array tracking selected options: `responses: Record` mapping `questionId -> score`. * **Browser Navigation Hook (`popstate`):** * Advancing a step must execute `history.pushState({ currentStep: stepIndex }, '')`. * Wire up a global listener to `window.addEventListener('popstate', (event) => { ... })`. If `event.state` contains a valid step index, mutate the step index state dynamically to prevent the default browser mechanism from completely dumping the session back to the splash page. * **Progress Tracking:** Display an instantaneous fraction progress indicator calculated dynamically as `(currentStep + 1) / 12`. ### Scoring & Form Dispatch Pipeline On the final question pane, render a standard lead capture container gathering Email and First Name. Upon clicking "Submit", the component must perform a `fetch` request payload execution to `/api/quiz-submit`: ```json { "email": "prospect@domain.com", "firstName": "John", "quizSlug": "ai-tsunami", "responses": { "q1": 3, "q2": 1 } } ``` --- ## 5. Backend Logic & Integrations ### API Processor (`src/pages/api/quiz-submit.ts`) The server-rendered API route processes the incoming responses against the quiz definition: 1. Fetch data directly from the dynamic Content Collection using Astro's `getEntry('quizzes', body.quizSlug)`. 2. Compute **Absolute Total Score** ($\sum \text{selectedScores}$). 3. Compute **Per-Section Sub-scores** ($\sum \text{selectedScores}$ categorized by `section` keys). 4. Identify matching **Outcome Tier** using boundary validation (`totalScore >= minScore && totalScore <= maxScore`). 5. **Cakemail Syncer:** Execute an authenticated server-to-server REST command or webhook mutation to Cakemail. Map sub-scores and the final tier configuration parameter cleanly into custom merge fields (e.g., `CUSTOM_SUB_INFRA`, `CUSTOM_TIER`). 6. Return a payload response containing JSON feedback tracking the payload outcome, or execute a direct 302 redirect string to `/quiz/results?tier=X&infra=Y&team=Z`. ### Server-Rendered Results Rendering (`src/pages/quiz/results.astro`) The landing viewport uses pure SSR to eliminate client-side content flashing: ```astro --- import { getEntry } from 'astro:content'; const { searchParams } = Astro.url; const tier = searchParams.get('tier') || 'high-risk'; const entry = await getEntry('quizzes', 'ai-tsunami'); const { Content } = await entry.render(); ---

Your Evaluation Assessment

 ``` --- ## 6. Prompt Directive for Coding Agent Copy and paste this explicit instruction into your coding environment to initialize development: ```text "Act as a principal frontend engineer specializing in Astro, TypeScript, and Content Collections. Implement a performance-optimized, self-hosted quiz engine matching the provided engineering specification. Focus completely on building the: 1. Zod schema validation rules inside `src/content/config.ts`. 2. A single file example of the hybrid MDX questionnaire layout structure inside `src/content/quizzes/ai-tsunami.mdx`. 3. A client-side framework engine file (`QuizStepper`) managing responsive layouts, validation steps, custom scoring payloads, and history history.pushState state reconciliation. 4. An Astro backend endpoint file (`/api/quiz-submit.ts`) managing absolute/sub-score evaluation processing and mocking out the external Cakemail fetch webhook transaction safely. Write clean, modular code ensuring all styling utilizes native Tailwind CSS layout utilities. Avoid using heavy runtime JS libraries outside the specified architecture." ```

Looking at the spec — it's a solid design for your own use, but a few things need adjusting before it's community-shareable. The biggest tension is that the spec hardcodes Cakemail, a specific slug (`ai-tsunami`), and `.length(12)` questions — fine for you, but a community version needs to be quiz-agnostic and ESP-agnostic.

Before I draft anything, three decisions worth making upfront:

1. **Shape of the deliverable.** Two reasonable options:
   - **Astro integration / npm package** (`astro-quiz` or similar) — installable, with a config object for ESP adapters. More work, but the right shape for community reuse.
   - **Template repo** — clone-and-customize. Faster to ship, lower maintenance burden, but each user forks rather than upgrades.

2. **Framework for the stepper.** The spec lists `Svelte/tsx/vue` as alternatives. For community reach, Preact or vanilla TS as an Astro island is the lowest-friction choice (no extra framework dependency). Svelte is nicest to write but adds an install requirement for anyone using your component.

3. **ESP integration.** Replace the hardcoded Cakem
